request.prompt: Which humanoid robots are suitable for research?

result.text:
The most suitable humanoid robot for research depends on what you want to investigate: robotics, artificial intelligence, locomotion, manipulation, human–robot interaction, or autonomous behavior.

For a university laboratory or an R&D team, I would prioritize robots with:

Accessible APIs and SDKs (Python, C++, ROS 2).

Access to low-level motor and sensor control.

Support for reinforcement learning and imitation learning.

Cameras, depth sensors, IMUs and force/torque sensing.

Availability of simulation models (URDF, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim).

Research-friendly hardware and software documentation.

The ability to modify and deploy your own control algorithms.

Humanoid robots worth considering

1. Unitree G1

Best overall starting point

Compact, approximately 1.3 m humanoid.

Suitable for locomotion, balance, reinforcement learning, manipulation and embodied AI.

Python/C++ SDK and a growing developer ecosystem.

Simulation and learning-based control workflows.

My recommendation: G1 EDU rather than the standard base model, if you need secondary development and low-level research access.

Resources: Unitree GitHub · Manufacturer

2. Fourier GR-1 / GR-2

Best for full-size research

Human-scale body.

Whole-body motion control and locomotion.

Manipulation and human–robot interaction.

Multiple degrees of freedom and dexterous-hand configurations.

My recommendation: Consider this platform when experiments require human-scale reach, more complex manipulation or whole-body coordination.

Fourier Intelligence

3. Booster T1

Best for locomotion research

Compact humanoid.

Dynamic walking and balancing.

Reinforcement learning and sim-to-real experiments.

SDK and development resources.

My recommendation: Particularly interesting for bipedal locomotion, motion planning, control algorithms and RoboCup-related research.

Booster Robotics

4. PAL Robotics TALOS

Advanced academic research

Full-size torque-controlled humanoid.

Whole-body control and dynamic locomotion.

Advanced manipulation.

ROS-based research environment.

My recommendation: Excellent for established robotics laboratories with substantial budgets and expertise in control theory.

PAL Robotics

5. EngineAI PM01

Compact development-oriented humanoid.

Bipedal locomotion and balance.

Whole-body motion research.

Worth evaluating for custom control and learning-based approaches.

My recommendation: An interesting alternative to the G1, provided the specific configuration offers the low-level interfaces your lab needs.

EngineAI

The platforms above are not equally open. In particular, verify the exact hardware variant, SDK permissions, motor-control access, sensor streams and simulation support before purchasing. Unitree's official SDK repositories are a useful starting point, while academic work also highlights the trade-off between commercial convenience and full hardware/software control.
